newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian stocks mixed, bears to reign over market.
newsitem.headline: Croatian stocks mixed, bears to reign over market.

text.p: Croatian stocks were mixed in Wednesday's thin trade and market participants said a bearish trend was likely to continue for some time.
Overall, nine of 20 active stocks fell, three rose and eight ended flat. Turnover was halved at 3.0 million kuna and volume shrank to 5,770 from 7,524 units.
"Everything indicates further and steady downslide of prices and there seems to be no end to it," analyst Domagoj Grabovac of Fima brokerage told Reuters.
He said the trend might last until September due to generally poor liquidity and sharp price fluctuations which deter serious investors.
The tiny local market has been driven by orders of big foreign investors and has suffered lately in their absence.
"We are in a period of stagnation and I expect low volumes of trading," said Josko Milisa, trader at I.C.F. brokerage.

Chocolate maker Kras took the spotlight on Wednesday with the largest traded volume of 1,117 units. It was also the biggest gainer, closing five kuna higher at 410 kuna after a mixed trade betwen 408 and 415 kuna.
But Grabovac foresaw a general selling pressure in the market limiting Kras' rise.
Traders were also worried by a dip of food processor Podravka of 5.9 kuna to 269.9 on volume of 993 shares after days of steady slide, following rumours of a 1996 loss.
Podravka is due to release 1996 results later this month.
"Its fall is likely to continue," Josko Milisa of I.C.F. brokerage said.
Blue chips Zagrebacka Banka and Pliva pharmaceuticals held their ground and were seen as stagnating.

Zagrebacka's ordinaries were flat at 2,000 kuna while its GDRs rose to $33.68 from $32.63 at Tuesday's close in London, reducing the spread to a bare minimum. Traders expected this to depress demand in Zagreb and volume was already shrinking.
Pliva closed at 450 kuna after selling 1,096 units in a 445-455 kuna range.
Varazdinska Banka ordinaries were also flat at 39,900 kuna with only three shares sold and its bearer stock lost 50 kuna to 1,050 on a meagre volume of five.
Croatia Banka led the day's decliners, dipping 10 kuna to 130 kuna on volume of 159 shares.
Three of five active hoteliers fell and two were flat.
